Anziehen or Tragen? German A2 Clothing Verb Practice

Distinguish putting clothes on from wearing them. Practise anziehen as an action and tragen as a state, with separable-verb examples.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Anziehen describes putting a garment on; tragen describes wearing it afterwards. Compare Er zieht die Stiefel an with Er trägt die Stiefel den ganzen Tag. Sich anziehen means getting dressed, while a named garment can be the object of anziehen.

Common mistake to avoid

Anziehen separates in ordinary main clauses: zieht ... an. Tragen changes its stem vowel with du and er/sie/es: du trägst, er trägt.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Er zieht die Gummistiefel vor der Tür an.He puts on the Wellington boots by the door.
Worked example 2Bei der Arbeit trägt sie eine Schutzbrille.She wears safety glasses at work.
Worked example 3Das Kind zieht sich nach dem Duschen an.The child gets dressed after showering.
Worked example 4Im Winter tragen wir dicke Socken.In winter we wear thick socks.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose anziehen for the act of putting on clothing and tragen for wearing it. A separated an may already be supplied. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Vor dem Hinausgehen ___ ich meine Jacke an. (put on)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: ziehe

Anziehen separates into ziehe ... an.

Question 2. Du ___ heute ein grünes Hemd. (are wearing)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: trägst

The du form of tragen is trägst.

Question 3. Bitte ___ die Handschuhe an! (put on, du)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: zieh

The du imperative of anziehen is zieh ... an; ziehe is also possible.

Question 4. Im Labor ___ wir Schutzkleidung. (wear)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: tragen

Wearing protective clothing uses tragen.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
